- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, increase forecast slightly to reflect bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope in next 3–5 periods to avoid overshoot.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ peak), model often underestimates decline — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% in subsequent periods.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast is trending upward, check for lag — true price often moves faster than model; reduce forecast lead time by 1–2 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates upward moves after 7–10 days — apply upward bias of 1–3% in early forecast window if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
